Stated Claim / Post Context:
WATCH -- New Jersey Mayor Lunges at Resident Accused of Targeting His Family: 'I Just Basically Snapped'

A Republican mayor in New Jersey had to be restrained at a township council meeting Wednesday evening when he and a resident got into a verbal argument.
The post WATCH — New Jersey Mayor Lunges at Resident Accused of Targeting His Family: ‘I Just Basically Snapped’ appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
A Republican mayor in New Jersey had to be restrained at a township council meeting Wednesday evening when he and a resident got into a verbal argument.

The chaos erupted when Pemberton Township Mayor Matthew Bianchini (R) rushed toward Michael Sawka, who has been a vocal critic of the mayor, Fox News reported Thursday.

Video footage showed Sawka gesturing towards the back of the room, where Bianchini’s wife and children were sitting, with his hand while he remained in his seat, then apparently waving his middle finger at the mayor.

Moments later, Bianchini got up and pointed at Sawka before moving towards him as those present tried to restrain the mayor:

Bianchini told the man, “I’m getting you,” before he was taken out of the room, ABC 7 reported Thursday. He later said, “I just basically snapped. I hate to put it this way, but it’s a long time coming,” and also admitted he was wrong to say he was going to get the man.

Sawka was accused of making rude comments toward the mayor’s wife and daughter, who were seated in the back of the room during the meeting, but Sawka has denied saying anything to them, per the ABC article.

More video footage showed Sawka saying “I want the police to arrest him now. I’m charging him with assault. He came here to threaten me physically, and he just said he’s gonna get me. That’s a threat!”

Bianchini also said his own actions were wrong, but added he would do it again if forced. “Don’t attack my family. I think any good husband, any good father, would’ve done just what I did,” he continued.

The mayor accused Sawka of harassing him and his family online and in person, but Sawka claimed he wanted to show others what he alleged was the government’s waste of money, while also claiming the mayor’s family targeted him online.

Sawka has filed a complaint seeking assault and terrorist threats charges in the case, but law enforcement has not said if charges will be pursued.

Bianchini claimed Sawka has “been a thorn in this township’s side” for years.

According to a New York Post report, “Bianchini is up for election this year, facing a challenge from Democrat Belinda Fontanez, and Republican Councilman Dan Dewey, who is mounting a write-in campaign.”

A romantic camping getaway in the New Jersey woods allegedly turned into a nightmare when a Bergen County man burned his girlfriend and abandoned her in the wilderness, authorities say.

Justin D. Martin, 36, of Saddle Brook, faces attempted murder and aggravated arson charges following the horrifying Oct. 15 attack in the Colliers Mills area of Plumsted township.

According to court documents, the badly injured woman managed to find a worker in the woods and desperately begged him to call 911.

The call came at 1:36 pm.

She told the worker her boyfriend had tried to kill her and burn her before fleeing in a Chrysler 200, according to the court reports.

Emergency crews found the woman conscious but suffering from burns and smoke inhalation.

She was intubated and flown to Temple University Burn Center in Philadelphia, where she was later reported in stable condition.

Investigators say the victim’s mother told detectives Martin had previously been verbally abusive and thrown objects at her daughter and even abandoned her at Freehold Raceway Mall, according to Patch.com.

During the prior incident, a stranger reportedly helped the stranded woman arrange a trip to her mother’s home.

On the morning of the alleged camping attack, the woman stopped at her mother’s home around 9 a.m. to collect camping supplies.

She never revealed where she was headed.

Hours later, Martin allegedly called the girl’s mother, claiming he and her daughter had argued and he had left the campsite, according to court papers.

Soon afterward, the mother received a devastating call from emergency responders saying her daughter was seriously injured.

Investigators tracked Martin’s Chrysler to Asbury Park, where they found the vehicle covered in evidence of sandy terrain, according to Patch.com

Police later located Martin with another man and a woman inside the vehicle.

The second man claimed he had been sleeping in the back seat all day and knew nothing about the attack. Detectives ended his interview, citing a lack of cooperation.

Martin declined to speak with investigators and requested and attorney.

He was arrested Oct. 16 and, according to Ocean County Prosecutor Bradley Bilheimer, is being held in Toms River at the Ocean County Jail.

The victim is in stable condition, said Bilheimer, and the investigation is ongoing.

Jersey’s sprawling Pine Barrens is the home of the mythical creature, the Jersey Devil.
